title: Hate Personified: Investigating the role of LLMs in content moderation

bias_targets.methodology: Prefixing prompts with specific country or language origins (e.g., 'The following statement was made in <country>') and measuring the Inter-Annotator Agreement (IAA) between the LLM's hate speech predictions and actual human annotators from those regions.
Prompting LLMs to adopt different gender personas (Male, Female, Non-binary) and measuring the variations in the Predicted Hate Label Ratio (PHLR) and IAA.

Prompting LLMs to adopt different racial/ethnic personas (Asian, Black, Hispanic, Middle Eastern, White, French/Mediterranean descent) and evaluating differences in their hate speech annotation rates.
Prompting LLMs with political orientation personas (Liberal, Independent, Conservative) to observe variations in hate speech prediction ratios and agreement with ground truth.

Prompting LLMs to assume various religious identities (Christian, Buddhism, Islam, Judaism, Hinduism, Irreligious) and comparing how these personas influence the frequency of labeling text as hateful.
Prompting LLMs with personas representing different education levels (ranging from <High School to PhD) and measuring the impact on hate speech classification metrics.
Prompting LLMs with upper-caste versus lower-caste personas for Hindi text to measure differences in the Predicted Hate Label Ratio.
Prompting LLMs with native versus non-native speaker personas (specifically for German text) and measuring differences in the Predicted Hate Label Ratio.

Prefixing prompts with fictitious numerical voting statistics (e.g., 'labeled hateful by <z>% annotators') to evaluate if the LLM's zero-shot classification is manipulated by irrelevant numerical anchors.
